title: Pixel Persona & Raster Brush Dynamics in Designer
subtitle: Persona Switching, Brush Categories, Flow vs Opacity & Jitter Engine

learningObjectives: Understand the hybrid architectural engine of Affinity Designer and switch between Vector and Pixel Personas seamlessly.
Distinguish between vector stroke brushes (Designer Persona) and true raster pixel brushes (Pixel Persona).
Master brush context dynamics: Width, Hardness, Spacing, and the crucial distinction between Opacity and Flow.
Configure the Brush Engine 'More' dialog: Size Jitter, Accumulation, Wet Edges, and Pressure controller response.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: In traditional illustration, artists were forced to choose between rigid mathematical vector software (clean lines, but flat mechanical shading) and raster painting applications (rich organic texture, but pixelation and un-scalable edges). Affinity Designer fundamentally solves this dichotomy by embedding a full raster painting engine directly inside the vector application via the Pixel Persona. Switching personas does not convert or rasterize your document; it simply exposes dedicated raster tools (Paint Brush Tool 'B', Eraser 'E', Selection Brushes) operating on pixel layers that coexist directly alongside vector bezier curves.

technicalEvidence.source: Affinity Designer 3.3.3 Persona Architecture & Pixel Brush Engine Specification

shortcut.win: Click Pixel Persona icon (Top-Left) / Custom shortcut in Edit > Preferences > Shortcuts. Tool: B (Paint Brush), E (Eraser), [ / ] (Size)
shortcut.mac: Click Pixel Persona icon (Top-Left) / Custom shortcut in Affinity Designer > Settings > Shortcuts. Tool: B (Paint Brush), E (Eraser), [ / ] (Size)

toolAndFeatureExplanation.description: Raster painting environment within Designer providing pressure-sensitive brush engines, textured grain, and raster selections. Note: Affinity Designer does not assign default keyboard shortcuts for persona switching out of the box.
contextBarOptions: Width input & scrub slider (Adjustable via [ and ] square brackets)
Opacity slider: Sets the maximum ceiling opacity for a complete stroke
Flow slider: Sets the rate at which pigment accumulates with overlapping passes (best at 10%–25% for grain)
Hardness slider: Controls radial edge softness (Shift+[ and Shift+])
More Button: Opens deep brush dynamics (Size Jitter, Flow Jitter, Spacing, Texture nozzles, Shape dynamics)

stepByStepInstructions.title: Switch to the Pixel Persona
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Open or create a document set to 300 DPI. Click the second icon on the top-left Persona toolbar (Pixel Persona), or press your custom shortcut if configured in Preferences > Keyboard Shortcuts. Observe the left toolbar reconfiguring to raster tools.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Open Brushes Studio & Select Dry Media
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: In the right studio dock, open the Brushes Studio. Notice the brush categories have changed to raster packs. Select the 'Dry Media' or 'Texture' category, and choose a textured stipple brush such as 'Chalk Rough'.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Calibrate Flow vs Opacity for Velvety Grain
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Select the Paint Brush Tool (B). In the Context Bar, set Opacity to 100%, but reduce Flow to 20%. Set Hardness to 0%. This ensures pigment builds up gradually like analog dry chalk without harsh brush stamp edges.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Configure Pressure Dynamics via More Dialog
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Click the 'More' button in the Context Bar. In the Brush Dynamics dialog, set Size Jitter to 25% and set Controller to 'Pressure'. Set Flow Jitter to 15% with Controller set to 'Pressure'. Click Close.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Paint a Multi-Pass Stippled Gradient
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: On a new pixel layer, make light, repeated passes with your stylus or mouse. Notice how repeated overlapping strokes build from a light speckle into a dense, velvety dark core shadow.

visualExamples.title: Opacity vs Flow Accumulation Matrix
visualExamples.description: Comparison of pigment delivery mechanics in Affinity's brush engine.
visualExamples.visualContent:
| Setting | Value | Behavior on Single Continuous Stroke | Behavior on Overlapping Multi-Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opacity Low / Flow 100% | Opacity 20%, Flow 100% | Never exceeds 20% opacity even if you scribble back and forth repeatedly | Only builds darker if you lift the stylus and start a brand-new stroke |
| Opacity 100% / Flow Low | Opacity 100%, Flow 20% | Builds continuously darker with every back-and-forth scrub (Analog behavior) | Seamless, velvety gradient transitions with beautiful textured grain |

guidedPractice.title: Calibrating a Custom Grain Shading Brush
guidedPractice.taskDescription: Duplicate a standard dry media brush, configure custom grain dynamics, and paint a 5-step tonal value sphere.
checkpoints: Switch to Pixel Persona by clicking the Pixel Persona icon on the top-left Toolbar.
Duplicate 'Chalk Rough' in the Brushes Studio and rename it 'Custom_Velvet_Grain'.
Open brush settings: set Spacing to 18%, Size Jitter to 20% (Pressure), Flow to 15%.
Draw a circular raster ball and paint a smooth shadow transition from white highlight to deep core shadow.
Verify that no individual brush nozzle stamp edges are visible at 100% zoom.
guidedPractice.expectedOutcome: A customized, responsive grain brush that delivers buttery, tactile shading transitions across broad surface areas.

independentChallenge.title: Textured Vector Moon Illustration
independentChallenge.prompt: Construct a stylized celestial poster: (1) In Designer Persona, draw a perfect vector circle (600x600 px) filled with midnight navy (#0F172A); (2) Switch to Pixel Persona; (3) Add a pixel layer and select a stipple noise brush; (4) Configure Flow to 20% and paint a dramatic crescent shadow curving around the sphere; (5) Add a secondary warm gold rim highlight along the opposite edge; (6) Switch back to Designer Persona and overlay sharp vector crater rings (1.5pt white strokes).

commonPitfalls.mistake: Leaving Flow at 100% and trying to shade by dropping Opacity.
commonPitfalls.consequence: Produces harsh overlapping banding streaks wherever the brush overlaps itself on a single stroke.
commonPitfalls.solution: Keep Opacity at 100% and lower Flow to 15%–25%. This allows pigment to accumulate naturally with smooth gradients.

commonPitfalls.mistake: Working in a 72 DPI document and wondering why raster grain looks blurry and pixelated.
commonPitfalls.consequence: At 72 DPI, raster brush stamps have very few pixels, turning subtle noise textures into chunky pixel squares.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always ensure your document is set to 300 DPI (or minimum 144 DPI for Retina web) in Document Setup.

commonPitfalls.mistake: Attempting to edit vector curves while still in the Pixel Persona.
commonPitfalls.consequence: The Pen and Node tools are unavailable; users get confused thinking their vector paths have locked.
commonPitfalls.solution: Click the Designer Persona icon on the top-left Toolbar to return to vector editing and manipulate nodes and shapes.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the primary difference in behavior between lowering Opacity versus lowering Flow when painting with a raster brush?
options: Opacity changes the brush color, while Flow changes the brush size.
Low Opacity caps the maximum density on a single stroke regardless of scribbling; low Flow allows pigment to accumulate continuously with overlapping passes.
Flow only works with a tablet stylus, while Opacity only works with a mouse.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Opacity sets a hard ceiling on transparency for an entire stroke, whereas Flow regulates the deposition rate per stamp, allowing you to build rich, multi-pass gradients by scrubbing over an area.

knowledgeCheck.question: How do you switch into the Pixel Persona in Affinity Designer by default?
options: Click the Pixel Persona icon on the top-left Toolbar (Affinity has no default shortcut out of the box, but custom shortcuts can be set in Preferences > Keyboard Shortcuts)
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Affinity Designer does not assign default keyboard shortcuts for switching between Personas out of the box. Users switch by clicking the persona icons on the top-left toolbar, or by assigning custom shortcuts in Preferences > Keyboard Shortcuts.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is document DPI critical when working with the Pixel Persona inside Affinity Designer?
options: Vector paths cannot be drawn in documents below 300 DPI.
Raster brush strokes created in the Pixel Persona are resolution-dependent bitmaps rendered at the document's DPI setting.
The Pixel Persona will automatically delete all layers if DPI is changed.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: While vector bezier paths scale infinitely without pixelation, pixel brush strokes are raster bitmaps tied directly to the document's resolution; low DPI results in blurry or chunky grain.

keyTakeaways: The Pixel Persona embeds a full raster painting engine directly inside the vector workflow.
Personas have no default shortcuts out of the box; switch via top-left icons or assign custom shortcuts in Preferences.
Low Flow (15%–25%) is the secret to velvety, non-banding analog grain shading.
Always design at 300 DPI for high-resolution print and crisp Retina raster reproduction.

slides.title: The Hybrid Engine: Pixel Persona in Designer
slides.subtitle: Unifying Vector Precision with Analog Texture
bullets: Pure vectors can feel sterile, cold, and mathematically rigid.
Pure raster software loses sharp scalability when resized for print or large formats.
Affinity Designer embeds an uncompromised raster painting studio via the Pixel Persona.
Switch personas in 1 keystroke without converting, exporting, or flattening layers.
slides.proTip: The document remains a live .afdesign file with simultaneous vector and pixel layers.

slides.title: Persona Navigation & Toolbar Adaptations
slides.subtitle: Seamless Workflow Switching
bullets: Designer Persona (Top-Left Blue Pen): Pen, Node, Shapes, Boolean tools.
Pixel Persona (Top-Left Brush): Paint Brush, Pixel Tool, Eraser, Smudge, Selections.
Export Persona (Top-Left Slices): Slices, batch multi-density exports.
No default persona shortcuts exist out of the box; assign your own in Edit > Preferences > Shortcuts.
slides.proTip: Configure custom shortcuts like Alt+1 / Alt+2 (or Opt+1 / Opt+2 on Mac) for rapid persona toggling.

slides.title: Raster Brushes Studio Architecture
slides.subtitle: Exploring Texture, Dry Media & Inks
bullets: In Pixel Persona, the Brushes Studio displays high-resolution raster brush categories.
Dry Media: Chalks, charcoals, and pastels with rich tooth and organic grain.
Inks & Gouache: Smooth pigment with natural brush edge textures.
Spray and Spatters: Realistic airbrush mist and stipple noise dispersion.
slides.callout: Vector brushes in Designer Persona stretch along curves; Pixel brushes deposit real pixels!

slides.title: The Golden Rule of Shading: Flow vs Opacity
slides.subtitle: Building Smooth, Velvety Texture Gradients
bullets: Setting Opacity to 20% creates a flat ceiling: you cannot build depth without lifting the pen.
Setting Flow to 15%–25% mimics real chalk: scrubbing back and forth deposits more pigment.
Overlapping low-flow strokes creates continuous, rich transitions with zero harsh lines.
Keep Opacity at 100% and regulate density exclusively via the Flow slider.
slides.proTip: Press number keys (e.g. '2' for 20%, '5' for 50%) to change Flow instantly while painting.

slides.title: Deep Brush Dynamics: The More Dialog
slides.subtitle: Pressure Sensitivity & Organic Jitter
bullets: Click 'More' on the Context Bar to open granular brush configuration.
Size Jitter: Randomizes brush diameter slightly, breaking mechanical regularity.
Flow Jitter: Varies pigment release based on graphics tablet stylus pressure.
Spacing: Set to 15%–20% for continuous smooth strokes without discrete dot stamps.
slides.proTip: Set Controller to 'Pressure' on Size and Flow for natural calligraphic hand response.

slides.title: Resolution Governance: The 300 DPI Standard
slides.subtitle: Why Vector Documents Need DPI Awareness
bullets: Vector shapes are infinite math; raster brush strokes are pixel arrays.
At 72 DPI, grain brushes look chunky, blurry, and pixelated when printed.
Always initialize illustration projects at 300 DPI in File > New or Document Setup.
At 300 DPI, grain textures reproduce with microscopic, velvety analog fidelity.
slides.callout: You can change document DPI anytime in File > Document Setup... without distorting vectors.
